title: Service Resilience Testing Tool (SRTT)
subtitle: Service Resilience Testing Tool
tour_step0_body:
This tool (Service Resilience Testing Tool) helps you observe DNS queries and connection footprints from apps on your phone, using tables, stats, and a map to see whether traffic leaves your region and which services are involved. Next we'll briefly explain DNS setup and how to start analysis.

Press Skip the tour to jump straight in, or Next to walk through the UI step by step.
tour_step1_body: Change your phone's DNS server to the IP shown in the card above (e.g. 203.0.113.42). After that, outbound DNS lookups from your apps can pass through this service and be recorded.
tour_step2_title: Step 2: Enter public IP, pick brand, start
tour_step2_body: Enter your phone's public IPv4, select the phone brand, then press Start analysis. Records will be tied to your source IP and appear below in real time.
tour_step3_title: Step 3: View the map and data
tour_step3_body: While monitoring, query rows stream into the table and the map and side stats update so you can follow connection patterns.
about_what_desc: SRTT (Service Resilience Testing Tool) is an open-source service resilience testing tool by OCF (Open Culture Foundation). It helps users see which domains their apps connect to and whether traffic flows through foreign servers — a starting point for digital sovereignty observation.
about_bullet_1: Real-time DNS query tracking with geographic visualization
about_bullet_2: Identify foreign traffic and cloud providers
about_bullet_3: Open Source · No user data stored
about_how_desc: Once you point your device's DNS server to this system, all domain name resolution requests are routed through here. The system will:
about_how_1: Forward queries to upstream DNS resolvers (e.g., 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8)
about_how_2: Tag destination IPs with country, city, and ISP via GeoIP database
about_how_3: Identify applications using a three-tier recognition engine
about_how_4: Verify foreign traffic confidence through latency probing
about_how_5: Push results to the browser dashboard in real-time via WebSocket
about_privacy_desc: All data is stored exclusively in server memory (Ring Buffer) with no database or disk writes. All data is destroyed upon service restart, ensuring zero data retention risk.
about_tech_frontend: Frontend: React 19 + TypeScript + Zustand + MapLibre GL
hero_description: Follow the steps once to change your phone's DNS. After that, we turn app internet activity into a simple list and map—so you can see which sites are involved and which countries those connections touch.
dns_server_ip_hint_link: How do I change my phone's DNS?
dns_hint_modal_title: How do I change my phone's DNS?
dns_hint_modal_step1: Install the “DNS Changer” app from the store links below (Google Play for Android, App Store for iOS).
dns_hint_modal_step2: Open the app, enter the DNS IP shown in step 1 on this page, then tap Start to apply it.
source_ip_hint_link: How do I find my phone's public IP?
source_ip_hint_modal_title: How do I find my phone's public IP?
source_ip_hint_modal_step1: On your phone, open myip.com.tw in the browser.
source_ip_hint_modal_step2: The numbers shown on that page are your public IP. Enter that value in the public IP (IPv4) field above.
brand_auto_tooltip: Inferred from live DNS queries, match score {{score}}
monitoring_disabled_desc: Monitoring is disabled. Enter your phone Public IP above and press Start.
pinned_section_hint: Selected records are kept here, safe from live data flow
pinned_limit_reached: Pin limit reached (max {{max}}). Uncheck some rows first.
report_snapshot_no_monitor: Monitoring controls are disabled in report view
shared_report_desc: This is a captured snapshot. Real-time updates are disabled.
table_empty: No records match the current filter
table_empty_hint_no_ip: Enter your phone Public IP in the toolbar above to start monitoring
merge_duplicates_tooltip: Collapse rows by application name (falls back to Domain), with occurrence count
confidence_low: Unable to probe; inferred from GeoIP database
inferred_app_heuristic: App name inferred from domain heuristic, not matched by exact rule
country_anycast_hint: This IP is an Anycast address served by {{provider}}; GeoIP cannot pinpoint a single country.
inferred_os: OS inferred from DNS query domain patterns, may not be fully accurate
inferred_geoip: Country data estimated from GeoIP database, may differ from actual location
inferred_foreign: Foreign status based on GeoIP database and latency probing, not 100% accurate
dns_setup_windows: Network Settings > Ethernet/Wi-Fi > Change adapter options > TCP/IPv4 > Preferred DNS
dns_setup_macos: System Settings > Wi-Fi/Network > DNS > Add the IP above
dns_setup_linux: Edit /etc/resolv.conf, add nameserver <IP>, or configure via NetworkManager
dns_setup_mobile: Wi-Fi settings > Long press network > Modify > Static IP > DNS: enter IP above
trace_hero_subtitle: The map shows an illustrative line from the default probe country to the destination. The hop table below is simulated and does not reflect the real network topology.
trace_await_hint: Enter a domain or IP, then run trace to see the illustrative path and hop list.
traceroute_no_data_hint: Click the Zap icon on a Result IP to start
traceroute_page_no_params: No target or shared data provided
report_note_1: This report is generated by SRTT (Service Resilience Testing Tool) for personal observation.
report_note_2: Country info comes from MaxMind GeoIP DB and may be imprecise; ASN/ISP reflects BGP routing ownership.
report_note_3: The report data is shared via URL encoding — no backend server stores it.
map_empty_hint_no_ip: Please set a monitoring IP first
map_empty_setup_hint: Enter your phone Public IP in Step 2 above and press Start analysis
